headline: Clean-box coder-30b decode measured 0.80 tok/s median against a 38.58 tok/s same-configuration baseline — roughly 48x slower. Cause NOT established.
operational_consequence: This is why dispatch run 20260831-003919-bd produced nothing. All three candidates of implement-photo-bio-section were killed by the ACP idle breaker (acp.idle_sec = 600) after reading the operator's content files and beginning to write index.html. At 0.8 tok/s a ~3000-token page takes ~62 minutes of unbroken generation, and a single long file write emits no intermediate step — so the watchdog cannot distinguish it from a hang. The coder was not stuck; it was generating.
what_was_ruled_out: Contention — the clean runs above have nothing else on the box.
Memory pressure — 7.33 GiB free, no page thrash.
Wrong OVMS version — 2026.2.5e9dcfc46 confirmed, the rolled-back build.
Kernel-cache recompilation — zero cache writes observed over 15 minutes.
CPU fallback — 17.79 GiB of GPU shared memory is allocated, so the model is resident on the GPU.
An OVMS-reported error — logs are clean; it reports 'Available devices: CPU, GPU, NPU' and proceeds with no warning or fallback notice.
not_established: The cause. Two candidates, not separated: (a) GPU driver/device state degraded by this session's OVMS version round-trip (2026.2 -> 2026.3 -> 2026.2, with the GPU-plugin OFFLOAD_RATIO property exercised and 33 kernel-cache entries quarantined); (b) a pre-existing condition never noticed because nothing re-measured since 2026-06-29 — which would be consistent with docs recording web coder tasks at 40-85 minutes each.
why_b_matters_if_true: If throughput has been at this level for some time, then the coder fleet's record (1 clean website in 46 attempts) is partly a SPEED problem misread as a quality problem: every candidate racing a 600 s idle watchdog it cannot beat on a long file write. That reframes the instrument-honesty arc and is worth settling before more coder-quality work is done.
next_step: Reboot, then re-run this exact probe. ~38 tok/s implicates driver state from this session; ~0.8 tok/s makes it pre-existing and the more important finding. Either answer is cheap to obtain and neither should be guessed at.
honest_limits: N=3, one warmup, 128-token generations, single prompt, no cooldown discipline, no prefill measurement, no GPU-engine profiling beyond coarse Windows counters. Sufficient to establish that a large regression exists against a directly comparable baseline; insufficient to attribute it.
